title: edge token stale window enables tenant impersonation during refresh failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A production incident where an edge proxy cache and token-refresh race allowed a short stale-window where requests were accepted with an old apikey->org binding. In multi-tenant flows this could be chained into cross-tenant request execution during failover/rotation windows. Affects Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that use the legacy session-cache fast-path on proxies.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two orgs (OrgA, OrgB) and an API key bound to OrgA.
2) Trigger a key rotation or revocation for the API key in the auth service.
3) Fire concurrent long-lived requests from a client while proxy nodes/edge are in mid-rollover (simulate connection drain).
4) Observe that some requests routed to a warm proxy node still using the old local cache mapping allowing calls with the old token to be accepted for ~10-60s.

5) If the downstream request performs a cross-tenant evaluation (e.g., replay of queued job referencing OrgB resources), the system accepts it under OrgA's prevously-cached identity leading to potential impersonation.
6) Reproduce reliably by replaying concurrent refresh and proxy drain under heavy request fan-out; test matrix includes hosted/dedicated/private network topologies.
Notes: reproduction requires simulating partial cache invalidation and connection reuse between proxy and runtime nodes.

mitigation_actions: Emergency: disabled legacy proxy session-cache fast-path for rotated keys in Hosted control plane (config flag: proxy.force_fresh_bind=true).
Advised Dedicated/Private customers to: apply config toggle, stagger rotation windows, and avoid simultaneous proxy drains during rotations.
Temporary increase of token binding TTL validation in runtime to require revalidation against auth service on node handoffs.
Added high-fidelity audit rule to flag apikey->org mapping changes with immediate request acceptance within 2 minutes of rotation.
root_cause: Local proxy cache accepted previous apikey->org mapping during a narrow window when the auth service had rotated/revoked the key but cache invalidation messages had not reached all proxy nodes. A race between connection draining, cached mapping re-use, and the token refresh flow allowed transient acceptance of stale bindings. The cache did not include a versioned binding signature, so there was no way to detect revocation without a synchronous round-trip.
fix_summary: Implement versioned apikey bindings and atomic refresh semantics: (1) attach a monotonic binding-version to apikey->org records; (2) require proxies to include binding-version in request headers and validate via lightweight signed binding token; (3) on rotation, increment version and publish invalidation messages; (4) fallback on mismatch to synchronous auth revalidation. Add unit/e2e tests and GA rollout plan.
deploy_notes: Canary rollout to 5% of edge fleet (region us-east-1) followed by metrics observation for 6 hours.
No DB schema changes required; publishing uses existing message bus (auth.invalidation-v2) with version field.
Rolling restart of proxy nodes required to pick up new signed-binding verifier; schedule with 5-minute stagger per rack.
Dedicated customers will receive a migration document and a one-click toggle in Console to opt into strict binding immediately.
follow_up_tasks: Add regression tests that simulate concurrent rotation + drain across hosted/dedicated/private topologies (ENG-259302).
Ship a Console flag to show active binding-versions per apikey for operators.
Security review and threat-model update for token lifecycle (schedule with security@redwood).
Revise runbook for key-rotation to require staged drains and validate full invalidation before rolling to next rack.
Backfill historical audit logs for the 48-hour window and notify impacted customers with timeline and remediation steps.
Instrument additional dashboards to surface binding-version churn and invalidation latency.
affected_customers: Several low-volume orgs reported anomalous cross-tenant traces during rotation window
